speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what types of jobs have been created by new investments brought in by EDB in the last three years; (b) how have the profiles of new investments changed and what are the anticipated trends in this area; and (c) how well is the local workforce positioned to benefit from the new investments in terms of skills and experience.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) how has the profile of investments in Singapore changed over the past 10 years; (b) given that electronics and biomedical manufacturing are the top two sources of investments in 2021, how well is our local workforce prepared for this growth; and (c) how can we continue to attract local talent in the electronics and manufacturing industries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: EDB attracts investments in a wide range of sectors including manufacturing, professional services and infocommunications and media.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Over the years, the profile of investments has moved towards higher value-added and innovation-focused activities, including in the semiconductor and biomedical manufacturing industries.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, best-in-class companies, such as GlobalFoundries, Arkema and Sanofi, have chosen Singapore for their new manufacturing investments.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We expect to attract more investments in advanced manufacturing, the digital economy and the green economy in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: We attract these investments so that Singaporeans can benefit from the jobs that these investments create and to secure our economic future and resilience.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Each investment strengthens our ecosystem and competitiveness, each investment creates more opportunities for firms to collaborate with one another, including between our SMEs and MNCs, and these, together, make Singapore more relevant to the world.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: One reason why companies choose Singapore is our talent pool of local and complementary global talent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) work closely with industry and the Labour Movement to equip our local workforce with relevant skills which companies need.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: By doing so, we can respond swiftly to the changing global economic landscape and opportunities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes help locals to take on jobs in growth areas, as well as in redesigned job roles due to technological changes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Government also works with larger companies to become "Queen Bees" by providing training opportunities for the whole ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Last year, Siemens also expanded their Advance Manufacturing Transformation Centre (AMTC), in partnership with JTC, SSG and other partners.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: AMTC will showcase Siemens' digital and industrial software, provide R&D platforms and resources for SMEs, expand training facilities and curricula to help upskill local and regional talent in Industry 4.0 capabilities.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Besides training, MTI has also been working with industry players and IHLs to make engineering and manufacturing careers more attractive to locals, as part of our Manufacturing 2030 strategy.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: More details will be announced in due course.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Even as we continue to grow our local timber, employers have provided feedback that they find it increasingly challenging to access the talent they require, especially in areas where there are skill shortages.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is a critical challenge we must overcome together, given the slowing growth in our local workforce and the aggressive competition posed by many cities and tech hubs for talent from all around the world.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To stay competitive and resilient, Singapore must remain open to complementary talent.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I would like to thank the Minister of State for his reply.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The first is: of the 54,000 jobs that were created in the last three years from the investments brought in by EDB, that Minister of State has mentioned, could he share, specifically, what is the percentage of these jobs that went to Singaporeans?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Also, related to that question is, for jobs where Singaporeans are currently without the skills or for areas where there are few qualified Singaporeans, how is EDB structuring the new investments such that firms are incentivised to tie the training of local staff and localisation of key positions to their business plans?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: However, this will, obviously, ultimately, depend on prevailing labour market conditions and also the ability of the companies themselves to identify suitable local talent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the Member's question how do we then encourage or put our local workforce in the best possible stead to take on these jobs, I want to assure the Member that we take a multi-pronged approach to ensure that Singaporeans can benefit from all of these investments and all of these jobs that are being created.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: EDB and other agencies, like ESG, SSG and WSG, partner our companies on initiatives to develop their workforce and to create better career pathways for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I also wanted to supplement this by saying that we regularly get feedback from companies on their challenges to find and also retain talent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Our agencies will continue their efforts to ensure that Singaporeans are equipped with the relevant experience and skills to seize these new opportunities that agencies like EDB bring in and create.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In fact, many of the investments that we attracted last year – for example, those from Global Foundries, Sanifi, Dell Technologies – are expected to be highly productive and also to operate with lean workforces.
